prompt: Implement the Singleton pattern: Config has a private constructor and a lazy getInstance() that always returns the same object, which stores settings in a private HashMap.
explanation: The private constructor blocks new Config() from outside, so the only way to obtain an instance is the static getInstance() gate. Lazy initialization means the static field starts as null and the object is built on the first request; every later call finds the field already set and returns the identical object, which the test proves with a reference comparison (a == b). Because there is exactly one instance, settings written through one reference are naturally visible through any other.
hints: You need a private static Config field -- static, because the single instance belongs to the class, not to any object.
In getInstance(), check whether the static field is still null; if so create the instance with the private constructor, then return the field.
set and get are thin wrappers over HashMap.put and HashMap.get; map.get returns null for missing keys, which is exactly what the spec wants.
